# CAB reader fixtures and boundaries

The CAB reader is an original pure Dart implementation. It uses the existing
MIT-licensed `koni_codecs` 0.9.0 `RawInflater` for raw DEFLATE; no native CAB
library or external program is an application dependency. It reads CAB version
1.3, one cabinet at a time, with stored or MSZIP folders. It does not run the
CAB executable-file attribute, install a package or authenticate a publisher.

## Primary format sources

- [Microsoft Cabinet Format](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/previous-versions/bb417343(v=msdn.10)),
  CFHEADER, CFFOLDER, CFFILE, CFDATA and checksum sections.
- [Microsoft MS-MCI structures](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/exchange_server_protocols/ms-mci/3048c471-f739-4d30-bcb3-a962cfe84a69),
  MSZIP framing and history retention.
- [RFC 1951](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc1951), DEFLATE framing.

MSZIP blocks each contain a complete DEFLATE stream but retain the preceding
32 KiB of the folder's decoded history. The reader seeds a fresh inflater with
that history using a non-final stored DEFLATE block, excludes the emitted prefix
from the result, and enforces a hard output bound. It requires the real stream
to terminate exactly and rejects trailing compressed bytes. Huffman tables are
not shared between MSZIP streams. CAB's checksum remainder bytes are folded
high byte first; complete four-byte words are little-endian. Reserved CFDATA
bytes are included in the header part of the checksum.

## Independent Windows MakeCAB fixtures

`reference-makecab-stored.cab` and `reference-makecab-mszip.cab` are byte-for-byte
UU-decoded copies of `libarchive/test/test_read_format_cab_1.cab.uu` and
`libarchive/test/test_read_format_cab_2.cab.uu` from
[libarchive commit d0bf2da07ebaa3964090ee936edea538d1602449](https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/tree/d0bf2da07ebaa3964090ee936edea538d1602449).
The original [test generator](https://github.com/libarchive/libarchive/blob/d0bf2da07ebaa3964090ee936edea538d1602449/libarchive/test/test_read_format_cab.c)
documents its Windows `makecab.exe /F mkcab1` and `makecab.exe /F mkcab2`
commands, input text and compression settings. Its BSD two-clause notice is
retained in [CAB_REFERENCE_LICENSE.txt](CAB_REFERENCE_LICENSE.txt).

Both fixtures include an empty file and `dir1/file1` and `dir2/file2` text
members. The MSZIP fixture additionally contains 33,000 zero bytes, spanning
two compression blocks. The Dart tests compare every member with the original
expected bytes and read entries in reverse order.

| Fixture | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `reference-makecab-stored.cab` | 266 | `0672797c111fca020fefe1b4b86de410f0eed36b52482a5bd282527392124d0e` |
| `reference-makecab-mszip.cab` | 245 | `c1a19b9c5f0d185079292ebb7ac0378e773d5ffd92e3b118c111178200064d85` |
| `reference-zlib-history.cab` | 32,983 | `348fd5d6ef387f8650d57e8ac47d98ccc6f341e16407bebaa2b9194903ccdb12` |

## Independent dictionary case and native readback

`reference-zlib-history.cab` is generated by the original
[check_archive_cab.py](../../support/check_archive_cab.py) script using Python
and zlib 1.3.2. The first block contains 32 KiB of deterministic SHA-256 counter
data. The second block repeats part of the first block using zlib's preset
dictionary; the generator asserts that decoding it without that dictionary
fails. This establishes a dictionary dependency rather than merely testing two
independently compressed blocks.

The script reads all three cabinets with system libarchive, compares every
member to its independently specified expected content, and prints the fixture
hashes. This run passed with libarchive 3.7.4. Native libarchive and Python are
test tooling only.

```sh
python3 test/support/check_archive_cab.py
# Optional regeneration of the original Python/zlib fixture:
python3 test/support/check_archive_cab.py --generate
```

The regular Flutter test suite uses committed fixture bytes and does not need
Python, libarchive, Windows or MakeCAB.

## Resource and compatibility boundaries

Metadata is limited to 16 MiB, names to 16 KiB, folders to 4,096 and CFDATA
records to 100,000. Each decoded folder is limited to 64 MiB by default, with
one folder cached at a time. Concurrent reads are serialized to preserve that
cache bound. The separate captured per-member read limit remains enforced even
if a caller requests a higher limit. Every compressed block is bounded to its
declared output and the 32 KiB MSZIP block limit.

Open reads headers, filenames and block descriptors; it does not decompress or
fetch member payloads. Reading any member verifies all present block checksums
in its folder. No checksum verification is claimed for a listed but unread
folder, a zero/absent checksum, or opaque application/signature data. Data ranges
cannot overlap the metadata or each other, and members cannot extend beyond
their folder. Source ownership is released on failed opens and exactly once
when a successful reader closes; pending reads are revoked on close.

Spanned cabinets, split blocks/files, Quantum, LZX and unknown compression flags
are refused. UTF-8 names and unflagged ASCII names are supported; unflagged
non-ASCII names are refused because CAB does not identify the legacy code page.
The existing member safety checks block traversal, absolute paths, drive/UNC
names, alternate data streams and control characters. CAB timestamps are local
wall-clock values without an encoded time zone; no UTC identity is asserted.
Creation and modification remain unavailable.

The focused suite also covers malformed lengths/counts/offsets, unsupported
attributes and versions, folder overlap, all truncated prefixes, corrupt
checksums, short sources, metadata/folder/member limits, MSZIP truncation and
trailing data, expansion beyond the declared length, reserved areas, UTF-8,
empty archives and files, multiple folders, out-of-order reads and close races.
